compute.reported_as: We estimated the ground state energy for the square-lattice J1-J2 model for linear cluster sizes L = 10, 12, 16. We used GCNNs with L layers, each consisting of six group-indexed feature maps. For most simulations, we performed 1000 SR steps using 1024 Monte Carlo samples, followed by 500 steps with 4096 samples. All simulations were carried out on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU.
compute.source: Sec. III A (training schedule); Sec. II C (single A100), arXiv:2211.07749 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: GCNN with L = 12 layers of six group-indexed feature maps; parameter count not stated. iterations = 1000 SR steps (1024 samples) + 500 steps (4096 samples) "for most simulations"; samples left null because two sample sizes are used in sequence. GPU-hours are stated only for the 16 x 16 lattice (approx. 300), not for this size.

compute.reported_as: The number of complex variational parameters in the RBM part is N_hidden for b_k and N_hidden x N_site for W_ik, respectively. As for the real variational parameters f_ij in the PP part, to reduce the number of parameters and the computational cost, we impose 4 x 4 sublattice structure for the 8 x 8, 12 x 12, and 16 x 16 lattices, and 6 x 6 sublattice structure for the 18 x 18 lattice [...] Then, the number of relevant f_ij parameters is 16(N_site - 1). [...] For each J2 point, we perform at least three independent optimizations of the RBM+PP wave functions from different initial variational parameters. [...] In the present study, we fix the number of hidden units N_hidden to be 16. We always apply the spin-parity and momentum projections during the optimization of the RBM+PP wave function. [...] we employ the sublattice structure in the f_ij parameters for the 8 x 8, 12 x 12, 16 x 16, and 18 x 18 lattices, to reduce the computational cost from O(N_site^4) to O(N_site^3) [...] The computation was mainly done at Supercomputer Center, Institute for Solid State Physics, University of Tokyo, and RIKEN supercomputers K and Fugaku.
compute.source: Nomura & Imada, Phys. Rev. X 11, 031034 (2021) = arXiv:2005.14142: Appendix A ('Calculation conditions'), Appendix B, Acknowledgments, arXiv:2005.14142 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Worklist lists the citing paper arXiv:2211.07749 (Roth, Szabo & MacDonald, Table I, 'Ref. [7]' column); the cost statements above are from the original Nomura & Imada paper (arXiv:2005.14142, fetched). No total parameter count is stated as a number: RBM part has N_hidden = 16 complex hidden-unit biases plus 16 x N_site complex weights, PP part has 16(N_site - 1) real f_ij parameters with the 4x4 sublattice structure (formulas only; not evaluated here). No sample count, iteration count, wall-clock, core count or per-run machine is stated; computing was done at the ISSP Supercomputer Center and on RIKEN K and Fugaku (CPU supercomputers). Implementation based on the mVMC package; optimizer SR.

corrections.reason: Settles VP10's question (quote of the published paper, or numbers Nomura shared?): the published PRX prints no 12 x 12 or 16 x 16 energy (only the 6 x 6 / 8 x 8 Table I, the 10 x 10 Table II and the 18 x 18 footnote [73]), and the only place it shows these sizes, Fig. 13, plots energies 1.7-3.2e-4 per site above Roth et al.'s "Ref. [7]" cells. Fig. 13 is, by the text's own list, produced without the point-group projection (only the momentum and spin-parity projections are "always" applied; the figures produced with the simplified point-group projection are named as Figs. 2, 6-10, 14-16, and Fig. 13 is not among them); its 6 x 6 and 8 x 8 points sit the same way above Table I (e.g. 8 x 8, J2 = 0.5: -0.4982865 vs -0.498886(1)). The Roth cells are therefore not a quote of the published paper but the "detailed numerical results from Ref. [7]" Nomura shared (Roth et al. acknowledgment), most likely point-group-projected states of the same method. Options for the ruling: this reference change (secondary, private communication printed in a peer-reviewed paper; peer_reviewed would follow the printing venue, PRB), or RULES.md 8 ("a cited number that cannot be found in the cited source is not admissible") if private communications are not admitted. Value and sigma are transcribed correctly from Roth et al. (VP10). Holds the instance record (2.2 combined sigma below Roth et al.'s own GCNN -0.496769(9); RULES.md 6 tie at 2 sigma): the ruling decides whether a private-communication number may hold it (precedent: the 10 x 10 CTWF -0.4976764(7), carried as known only by private communication).
